payload.question: This PayPal payment confirmation looks legitimate. Can you spot what's wrong?
payload.image_alt: A very convincing fake PayPal payment confirmation email
options: The 'Cancel and Get Refund' button uses a homograph URL: 'pаypal.com' with a Cyrillic 'а'
The transaction ID format looks different from real PayPal
The email greeting says 'Dear Customer' instead of your name
The payment amount ends in an unusual cent value ($247.93)
payload.anomaly_hint: Look extremely carefully at the domain in any links — some characters may not be what they appear

explanation: This is a homograph attack. The Cyrillic letter 'а' (U+0430) looks identical to the Latin 'a' (U+0061) in most fonts, but resolves to a completely different domain. Modern browsers show the punycode (xn--pypl-...) in the status bar for international domains. This is why hovering alone isn't sufficient — you need to inspect the actual URL encoding. Generic greetings are suspicious but don't prove phishing.
